command: Human AGFG2/HRBL (O95081) has physiologically relevant GTPase-activator activity, potentially toward an ARF substrate. Evaluate the molecular-function claim separately from its established vesicle-trafficking roles. The exact target retains Arg75, corresponding to ASAP3 Arg469, but carries Thr89 at the position aligned to ASAP3 Asp484. The existing reproducible MAFFT domain alignment records these coordinates. PMID23433073 proposes substantial catalytic divergence of AGFG domains including the Asp and conserved tryptophan positions, but explicitly also reports loss of the Asp-homologous site in all 18 GIT-family sequences. Primary PMID10788515 directly measures ARF GAP activity of GIT1 and GIT2, so this substitution cannot be assumed universally diagnostic of inactivity. Inspect primary structural/mutational PMID20510928 and relevant biochemical studies for whether the ASAP3 requirement generalizes to AGFG2 or reflects a particular catalytic mechanism. PMID34369554 calls an R75Q construct GAP-dead and states that it still promotes Weibel-Palade body secretion, with those data not shown; the secretion assay is not itself a GTPase-hydrolysis assay. Determine whether any direct AGFG2 biochemical evidence establishes retained activity, altered specificity or loss, and distinguish absent assays from functional refutation. Consider a noncatalytic trafficking-cofactor model without assuming that this role and GAP catalysis are mutually exclusive.
